s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal mass with mild discomfort during exercise
salient_findings: Painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography
key_facts: 16-year-old male with no prior medical history
Noted a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier
Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
Lump’s size remained unchanged over two months
Experienced mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
Painless mass on physical examination
Testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
Mass contained two small hypoechoic foci
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers were all within normal limits

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Most common epididymal tumor, matches clinical presentation of a painless scrotal mass

shortlist.label: Epididymal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign condition, consistent with ultrasonography findings of a well-demarcated hyperechoic mass

shortlist.label: Spermatocele
shortlist.why_kept: Benign cystic lesion, possible cause of a painless scrotal mass, although less likely given ultrasonography characteristics

shortlist.label: Papillary cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare benign tumor, could explain the ultrasonography findings and clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Epididymal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor, possible cause of a painless scrotal mass, although less common than adenomatoid tumor or epididymal cyst

raw.rationale: The presence of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic mass at the tail of the epididymis with two small hypoechoic foci, as seen on scrotal ultrasonography, is most consistent with an adenomatoid tumor, which is a common benign tumor of the epididymis in young men.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: Epididymal cysts are typically fluid-filled and anechoic on ultrasound, which does not match the solid, hyperechoic mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Spermatocele
rejected.why: Spermatoceles are cystic structures that contain sperm and are typically anechoic on ultrasound, which does not match the solid mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Papillary cystadenoma
rejected.why: Papillary cystadenoma is a rare tumor that is more commonly associated with the testicle or paratesticular tissues, rather than the epididymis.

rejected.label: Epididymal lipoma
rejected.why: Epididymal lipomas are rare and would typically appear as a hyperechoic mass on ultrasound, but the presence of two small hypoechoic foci within the mass is not typical of a lipoma.
